The paired m170 results in d1c43590b9e0a99ce3b8 and 1f21033e56ca247448e2, together with the m159 intermediate labels d3d2b36ec3417c1c1c6c and da1e48445e8e0b651070, support measuring transition regions rather than only extremes. The m209 result in 80f546c47198fa7c6dbf showed that a genuinely late finish can still be underpredicted, while m104, m120, m144, and m25 results in 302e458c5ed2285ca328, e4fd83fb3852eb354a66, 5ff3e81c102706da6a30, and d21f08a7e8eaa163ecfc showed that broad predicted intervals can also greatly overstate V2. The new batch therefore concentrates on scaffold-specific boundaries, includes matched loading probes for tail families, and adds compact and molecule-novel controls to limit global overcorrection.","batch_rationale":"The batch combines high-value failure repair for late V2 modes, local condition-response anchors, loading-sensitive experiments, and chemically distinct controls. The m118, m119, m125, m141, m146, m159, m160, m161, m170, m171, m177, m198, and m209 selections target nonlinear or broad-tail regions where measured outcomes have exposed transfer failures. The m72, m90, m11, m39, and m205 points extend response curves through intermediate regimes. Molecule-novel bromoester, diaryl-ketone, aromatic-ketone, and related controls test descriptor transfer, while compact m2, m45, m47, m48, m108, and m109 rows constrain corrections for ordinary chemistry. Together these labels should improve calibration of both V1 and V2 across the Row-distribution and help QGeoGNN learn when a tail is chemically specific, loading-driven, or absent."}
